title: Status and Freshness
summary: Choose current status evidence over obsolete summaries and low-value background.
learnerGoal: Curate a reviewable status package for an executive update.
taskAudience: VP reviewing a cross-functional project update
whyMatters: Status packages fail quietly when stale summaries look plausible and current facts are buried.
taskBrief: Prepare a concise AI-ready package that will help generate an executive status summary for Project Atlas. Prioritize the most current facts, preserve one key risk, and avoid background that does not change the summary.
successCriteria: Privileges current tracker evidence over stale summaries.
Keeps one material customer-impact risk visible.
Avoids duplicated or obsolete project background.
quickPredictionPrompt: What makes a status note feel current enough to trust?
dynamicFacts: Executive wants: one-paragraph status + risks + next step
Project Atlas is entering pilot rollout
outputContract: Return sections: Current Status / Key Risk / Immediate Next Step
Note uncertainty instead of smoothing it over

cards.title: Live Tracker Update — Today 9:15 AM
cards.excerpt: Pilot rollout is at 82%. One blocking issue remains in identity sync for a subset of users.
cards.summaryText: Most current delivery status and blocker.

cards.title: Customer Escalation Note — Yesterday
cards.excerpt: Two pilot users were delayed by the identity sync issue. Customer success requested a risk mention in the next executive update.
cards.summaryText: Current customer-impact signal tied to the blocker.

cards.title: Project Manager Weekly Summary
cards.excerpt: States rollout is on track and lists several completed workstreams. Written before the new blocker appeared.
cards.summaryText: Useful background summary, but no longer current enough to lead.

cards.title: Launch Plan v1.1
cards.excerpt: Old launch assumptions and milestone dates from before pilot scope changed.

cards.title: Standup Notes Clip
cards.excerpt: Notes mirror the live tracker and mention the same blocker in less precise language.
cards.summaryText: Mostly duplicate of the stronger tracker source.

cards.title: Architecture Overview
cards.excerpt: System context explaining identity sync dependencies. Helpful only if a reviewer needs deeper follow-up.
cards.summaryText: Useful for follow-up, not core status inclusion.

cards.title: Old Dashboard Export
cards.excerpt: Shows rollout at 67% from three weeks ago.

cards.title: Next-Step Owner Note
cards.excerpt: Identity team will release a fix candidate by tomorrow afternoon and validate with two pilot accounts.
cards.summaryText: Concrete immediate next step for the executive update.

cards.title: RCA Draft
cards.excerpt: Early root-cause detail for the identity sync issue. Too detailed for the core executive summary, but useful if asked how the blocker emerged.
cards.summaryText: Keep for conditional follow-up, not core summary.

commentary: Include the live tracker, current risk note, and immediate next step.
Summarize aging or duplicate context that helps but should not outrank current evidence.
Omit visibly stale exports and obsolete plans.
Retrieve deeper technical detail only if follow-up requires it.

bonusBranches.title: Stricter Budget Replay
bonusBranches.description: Tighten the budget and see whether your current package still protects the key status story.
bonusBranches.coachNote: Protect current status, current risk, and immediate next step. Everything else must earn a much smaller footprint.

overlayCards.title: Executive Channel Constraint
overlayCards.excerpt: Executive update must stay to one tight paragraph: current status, main risk, and immediate next step only.
overlayCards.summaryText: Compact output constraint for the strict-budget replay.

commentary: The stricter-budget replay should protect only the few cards that directly change the answer.
Compact replay-only constraint cards can shape the answer without demanding another full direct include.
Older background and follow-up material should move into Summarize, Retrieve Later, or Omit much earlier than in the core run.

bonusBranches.title: Authority vs Freshness Drill
bonusBranches.description: Re-run the mission while explicitly favoring the freshest evidence over aging summaries that feel comfortable but no longer lead.
bonusBranches.coachNote: Let the live tracker and yesterday's escalation note lead. Aging summaries can help, but they should never override the current blocker story.

overlayCards.title: Ops Monitor Snapshot — Today 10:05 AM
overlayCards.excerpt: The identity sync blocker is still open. No newer signal outranks it in the pilot rollout right now.
overlayCards.summaryText: Fresh monitoring evidence for the authority-versus-freshness replay.

commentary: The authority-versus-freshness replay should make current source-of-record evidence visibly lead the answer.
Branch-only fresh evidence should change what the best package looks like, not just how the coaching sounds.
Comfortable but aging summaries can support the answer, but they should not steer it.

compoundChecks.label: Current status stays bounded by 82% rollout, in-progress validation, and tomorrow-afternoon fix timing

groups.label: validation still pending
phrases: validate it with two pilot accounts

compoundChecks.teachingNote: Status answers fail when timing, completion state, and validation drift apart inside one polished summary.

reviewCoaching.message: Status answers should preserve current state, the live blocker, and the next-step timing instead of collapsing them into a finished story.
Percent complete, account count, and timing are the highest-risk status facts; preserve them exactly.
The rollout is still in progress, validation is still pending, and the fix candidate is still tomorrow afternoon. Keep those together.
